To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the in vitro dissolution of electrophoretically applied calcium phosphate coatings on titanium is strongly influenced by the phase composition of the coatings, which depends on the deposition conditions and the vacuum sintering temperature, and that the in vitro stability of the coatings can be improved by the use of calcium phosphate compositions containing magnesium.

the electrophoretic coating of a porous metal substrate with a CPC is hampered by adsorption of water and that the subsequent vacuum sintering results in a complex phase transformation and an increase of in vitro degradation.

the electrophoretic coating of porous titanium wire mesh with CPC is hampered by water adsorbed on the metal surface, and that the vacuum sintering of the ceramic film leads to the formation of oxyhydroxy- and tetracalium phosphates, with the latter being more soluble in vitro than hydroxyapatite.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model porous metal-CPO material system for the investigation of material factors.
the development of model porous metal coatings with CPC coating, which are characterized by a uniform porous structure.
the development of a model material for the investigation of material factors in porous metal-CPC systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of CPC coating on bone formation is not predictable.
the electrophoretic coating of OOWM with CPC is a suitable method for the fabrication of CPC-coated porous titanium implants.

electrophoretic coating of OOWM is a promising approach to obtain CPC-coated porous metals, and the material properties of the ceramic coatings are influenced by the deposition conditions and subsequent vacuum sintering.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrophoretic coating of porous metals with CPCs is feasible.
a uniform porous structure is a prerequisite for reproducible CPC coatings.
electrophoretic ceramic coating of porous metals is feasible and can lead to CPC-coated porous metals with a high degree of reproducibility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a CPC coating on a porous metal surface should be considered a composite material.
the structure and composition of CPC coatings on porous metals is influenced by the processing parameters.
a CPC coating is not always beneficial.
